newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda ends Chinese dam power deal.
newsitem.headline: Uganda ends Chinese dam power deal.

text.p: Ugandan authorities said on Thursday they had terminated an $84 million contract for Chinese firm Sietco to extend a hydro-electric power plant.
Uganda had in July suspended the contract to extend the British-built power plant at Owen Falls dam near the eastern Jinja town by Sietco, complaining of slow, shoddy work.
But officials said last month the government was reviewing the suspension after appeals from the Chinese government.

"After consultations with the main donors to the project, the government has decided to terminate the contract," the state Uganda Electricity Board (UEB) that is overseeing the extension work said in a statement on Thursday.
"The government has therefore decided to repossess the site of the works from Sietco," the Ugandan power monopoly added.
The contract was the Chinese company's biggest in Africa, its officials said, and it was funded mostly by the World Bank.
Sietco won the contract in November 1993, beating 12 other international firms. The project would raise capacity at the 160 megawatt station to 180 megawatts by September 1997,

Work at the station, 80 km (50 miles) east of Kampala, started in February 1994, but last year the Chinese company asked for 15 more months, saying it could not complete the work on schedule as it had run short of money.
Turning down the request, the Ugandan government also said it was not happy with the quality of Sietco's work.
Sietco officials complained they had run short of money because much of it had gone to Ugandan government officials who demanded bribes saying they had helped them win the contract.
Uganda is badly in need of extra electricity. Economists say the shortage is stalling economic growth. Current demand is 240 megawatts, and grows at 24 percent a year, officials say.
